name: # The executable cross-port divergence register (ADR-14).
# DIVERGENCE.md is the prose record and stays authoritative on WHY each
# split exists and what it costs. This file is what RUNS: every row is
# asserted by all runtime suites -- go/divergent_test.go reproduces `go`,
# ts/test/divergent.test.js reproduces `ts`, and the Rust runner reproduces
# `rust` -- so a divergence
# that gets FIXED fails here exactly as loudly as one that regresses, and
# the row must then be deleted. Prose cannot do that. The sibling repo
# has the scars: jsonic's differences doc claimed 2.e3 and 1e999 still
# diverged long after they were aligned.
# EIGHT tab-separated columns:
#   name           unique, kebab-case; the failure message names it
#   probe          `lex` or `spec` -- the closed observation set below
#   arg            a JSON object of probe arguments, or `-`
#   input          the source text
#   go             what the Go port produces TODAY
#   ts             what the TypeScript port produces TODAY
#   rust           what the Rust port produces TODAY
#   justification  why this is recorded rather than repaired
# A row here is an admission of parity debt, not a way to silence a
# failure. Repair the divergence if you can; register it only if you
# cannot, with a justification the next reader can act on. Every group
# carries a CONTROL row -- an adjacent case where the ports AGREE -- so a
# repair to the divergent row cannot be confused with unrelated breakage.
# WHY A PROBE COLUMN AND NOT jsonic's `input -> parse result`. This engine
# ships no grammar, so there is nothing to parse an input against by
# default, and its divergences are observed at several layers (token
# columns, token spans, decoded values, grammar install). The probe names
# which observation a row makes.
#   lex    Lex `input` under arg.opts. Select ONE token: arg.find (first
#          token whose src equals it) or arg.at (0-based index); default
#          index 0. Render the arg.show fields joined by `:`, from the
#          closed set name|src|si|ri|ci|valhex. If the lex FAILS first,
#          render ERROR:<code>:<col>:<src> instead.
#   spec   Install arg.spec -- a serialized GrammarSpec, either inline or
#          the name of an `# @spec` definition below -- under arg.opts,
#          then parse `input`. Without arg.show: OK:<value> or
#          ERROR:<code>. With arg.show (fields from code|pos|col|row): a
#          bare OK, or ERROR: plus those fields joined by `:`. A grammar
#          that will not load at all renders INSTALL_ERROR.
# SELECT ONE TOKEN, do not render the stream. The two ports emit
# different token SEQUENCES for the same source -- Go emits no #SP where
# TypeScript does -- so "the third token" is not the same token in each,
# and a whole-stream render would go red for a reason no row is about.
# arg.find is sequence-proof; prefer it.
# TWO RENDERING TRAPS, both already paid for once in this repo (#156):
#   Never use a runtime's own quoting. Go's %q and JavaScript's
#   JSON.stringify escape different characters, so a `src` rendered
#   through either diverges for reasons that are not a divergence. `src`
#   and string values render VERBATIM -- which means a row must not put a
#   tab, newline or carriage return in a column it renders.
#   Never use a runtime's own key order. The `spec` probe renders map
#   keys sorted by UTF-16 code unit in both ports (ADR-15 puts key order
#   out of contract, and UTF-16 vs UTF-8 order is itself a live split:
#   "10000" sorts before "e000" in one and after it in the other).
# ESCAPES: this repo decodes \n, \r, \r\n and \t in EVERY column, in both
# loaders (test/AGENTS.md). So a control character inside a JSON `arg`
# cell must be spelled \uXXXX -- a raw \n would be decoded to a real
# newline before JSON.parse ever sees it, and invalid JSON is the best
# case. A lone backslash is untouched, which is what lets a serialized
# regex be written here at all.
# COVERAGE: go/divergent_test.go asserts that every `### ` heading in
# DIVERGENCE.md is either an `# @divergence:` group below or an entry in
# that file's `notRegistered` map with a reason. An entry cannot be
# quietly dropped from the register, and an exemption cannot outlive the
# heading it exempts.
# Named spec definitions, referenced by `{"spec":"<name>"}`:

# @spec pushchainoff {"v":5,"options":{"rule":{"start":"__start__"}},"rule":{"__start__":{"open":[{"p":"mid"}],"close":[{"s":["#ZZ"],"a":"@bubble$"}]},"mid":{"open":[{"p":"arr"}],"close":[{"a":"@bubble$","r":"tail"}]},"arr":{"open":[{"a":"@array$","p":"elem"}],"close":[{"a":"@push$","k":{"push$":{"src":true,"chain":false}}}]},"tail":{"open":[{"s":["#CA"],"p":"elem"}],"close":[{"a":"@push$","k":{"push$":{"src":true,"chain":false}}}]},"elem":{"open":[{"s":["#NR"],"a":"@node$","k":{"node$":{"init":true,"nterms":1}}}],"close":[{"a":"@capture$"}]}}}

# @spec pushchainon {"v":5,"options":{"rule":{"start":"__start__"}},"rule":{"__start__":{"open":[{"p":"mid"}],"close":[{"s":["#ZZ"],"a":"@bubble$"}]},"mid":{"open":[{"p":"arr"}],"close":[{"a":"@bubble$","r":"tail"}]},"arr":{"open":[{"a":"@array$","p":"elem"}],"close":[{"a":"@push$","k":{"push$":{"src":true}}}]},"tail":{"open":[{"s":["#CA"],"p":"elem"}],"close":[{"a":"@push$","k":{"push$":{"src":true}}}]},"elem":{"open":[{"s":["#NR"],"a":"@node$","k":{"node$":{"init":true,"nterms":1}}}],"close":[{"a":"@capture$"}]}}}

# @divergence: Column positions for astral characters
astral-col-ascii-control
justification: Control row, not a divergence: throughout the BMP the two ports report the same column. Kept adjacent so a repair to the row below cannot be mistaken for unrelated breakage.

name: astral-col-astral
justification: Forced by the scan unit: TypeScript scans UTF-16 code units, so U+1F600 advances the column by TWO; Go scans runes and advances by one. Neither port can adopt the other's without changing what its lexer scans. The input is U+1F600, a space, and `y`.

name: # @divergence: Token offsets reach parsed values, not only diagnostics
token-si-ascii-control
justification: Control row, not a divergence: for ASCII input the two ports agree on Token.SI.

name: token-si-astral
justification: Go's Token.SI is a BYTE offset (4 bytes for U+1F600, plus the space); TypeScript's counts UTF-16 units (2, plus the space). Worse than the column split above because Token.SI is plugin API: a plugin that records it lands the scan unit in its OUTPUT, which is how @tabnas/c came to carry it in a CST span. Not repairable in a plugin.

name: # @divergence: Lone surrogates in quoted strings
surrogate-pair-control
justification: Control row, not a divergence: a well-formed surrogate PAIR agrees in every spelling. Three of those spellings were broken in Go until 0.8.4, so this is worth an assertion of its own.

name: lone-surrogate
justification: TypeScript preserves the unpaired code unit because JS strings are UTF-16 and permit it; Go folds it to U+FFFD, matching encoding/json. Each port does the right thing for its own string model. The cost is real -- Go conflates values TS keeps distinct, reported downstream as a lattice-law breach (aontu#24) -- so read DIVERGENCE.md before touching this.

name: # @divergence: An explicitly empty option cannot be expressed in Go
empty-chars-control
justification: Control row, not a divergence: with the default quote characters both ports lex a quoted string as #ST.

name: empty-chars
justification: String.Chars is a plain string in the Go options, so "" is its zero value and an explicitly empty value cannot be told from an unset one -- the default quotes stay in force and the input is still a string. TypeScript distinguishes '' from undefined and honours it, so the same text is ordinary text there. @tabnas/css shipped this in both ports. The repair is Chars *string, a breaking change across a published module, so it is a release-policy call rather than a parity fix -- see DIVERGENCE.md for the adoption count.

name: # @divergence: Regex dialect in serialized terminals
regex-ws-ascii-control
justification: Control row, not a divergence: the input is one U+0020, which JS \s and RE2 \s both match. A change here means something other than the dialect gap broke.

name: regex-ws-nbsp
justification: The input is one U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE. JS \s is Unicode-aware; RE2's is the Perl class [\t\n\f\r ], so Go rejects it. Mechanically repairable by a compile-time rewrite, at the price of this engine owning a regex-dialect translation layer for every downstream grammar in both runtimes -- a maintainer decision, not a mechanical fix.

name: regex-ws-ideographic
justification: The input is one U+3000 IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE. A second point of the same class gap, kept because a partial repair that widened RE2's class by a few code points would otherwise look like a full one.

name: regex-ci-ascii-control
justification: Control row, not a divergence: ASCII case folding agrees.

name: regex-ci-kelvin
justification: The input is one U+212A KELVIN SIGN. The gap runs the OTHER WAY here: RE2 case-folds by Unicode rules and matches it, while JS /i without /u does not fold it to `k`. Not repairable the way \s is -- RE2 has no ASCII-only folding flag, so matching JS would mean rewriting the pattern into explicit alternations.

name: regex-lookahead
justification: A harsher kind of divergence: not a different result but a grammar that will not LOAD. RE2 implements no lookahead, by design, and go/utility.go refuses the pattern at compile time. That is the right failure mode, and it still means a spec written and tested against TypeScript can be unloadable in Go.

name: regex-backreference
justification: The same install-time refusal for a backreference, which RE2 also omits by design. Kept separate from lookahead because the two are refused by different branches.

name: # @divergence: `@push$` with `chain: false` and a grammar that breaks its promise
push-chain-off
justification: @push$ with chain:false skips re-publishing the grown list back along the replacement chain. TypeScript and Rust hand out one array object, so every holder sees every element and the key is a no-op there; a Go slice is a value, so the rule the parent's Child still points at (`mid`, neither the list's owner nor the pusher) keeps the header it held when it was replaced. This grammar READS that rule, through __start__'s @bubble$, which is exactly what declaring the key promises not to do -- and the loader cannot check the promise. Recorded rather than repaired because repairing it means either removing the opt-out, which puts @push$ back to O(elements^2) on the shape @tabnas/json uses, or making the walk unconditional-but-cheap, which go/doc/differences.md records three blocked attempts at. The register is here so the cost is executable in all three suites rather than pinned in one Go unit test.

name: push-chain-on
justification: Control row, not a divergence: the same grammar with the key absent, where the chain walk runs and all three ports agree. A change here means something other than the opt-out broke.

name: # @divergence: Forward traversal of a replacement chain in Rust
chain-next-one-hop
justification: Control row, not a divergence: all three ports take `rule.child` to be the rule the parent PUSHED and its `next` to be the replacement that took its place, so the FIRST hop along the chain agrees. A change here means the child link itself broke, not the chain walk the two rows below are about.

name: chain-next-two-hops
justification: TypeScript and Go hold a replaced rule as a live object whose `next` goes on being written after the parent stopped looking, so walking `child.next.next` reaches the chain's third link. Rust holds a frozen record instead, taken when each link stopped being the current rule, and a link's `next_rule` is the successor as it stood at its CREATION, with no successor of its own yet. So the walk reaches one hop and then finds nothing, and the alternate falls through to the unconditional one. Repair direction: Rust changes, TypeScript defines the language and Go already agrees. Not repaired here because the forward link cannot be patched in place -- the successor's record is shared through an Rc by the time the grandchild exists -- and the mechanism that fixes it is item R7 / release note [V4] of doc/rust-callback-contract-spec.md, which resolves a chain link's successor from the live prev_rule chain rather than a stored forward pointer.

name: chain-next-three-hops
justification: The same gap one hop further out, where the canonical ports run off the end of the chain and back to the parent the tail popped to. Kept separate from the row above so a partial repair that restored one more hop cannot be mistaken for a full one.
